matchById.recapBody: [{"type":"header","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Atlanta completes epic comeback to claim inaugural TGL title","format":{"variants":["bold"]}}],"style":"h2","format":{"text-align":" center"}},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Billy Horschel practically floated across the Green, dropping his putter and throwing his hat in celebration after a 17-foot, 10-inch birdie putt gave Atlanta Drive GC its first lead of the night on the penultimate hole."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"It was the moment that helped Atlanta capture the SoFi Cup with a dramatic 4-3 victory over New York Golf Club in Match 2 of the best-of-three Finals Series."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"New York still had a chance at the 15th and threw the Hammer before Patrick Cantlay and Cameron Young hit their tee shots. An up-and-down for birdie from Cantlay sealed the deal and the celebration was on for the first-ever TGL champions."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“I hit the spot, it looked good. Two feet out I knew it was in the hole and I blacked out,” Horschel said of the lengthy birdie putt on No. 14. “I think I said some expletives. I think I said something about this being my house. It was a lot of fun.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"It was a dramatic and sudden end to the inaugural season. There would be no Match 3 Tuesday night."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Instead, Atlanta team owner Arthur Blank accepted the SoFi Cup trophy on a stage in the middle of the field of play. He thanked league co-founders Mike McCarley, Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy and said he was “privileged and honored” to have the first trophy before passing it down to Cantlay, Horschel, Justin Thomas, Lucas Glover and team coordinator Ben Helmrath."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Then the smoke machines went up and the confetti rained down and the celebration was on for Atlanta, which finished the season with a dominant 7-1 record."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"It was fitting that Horschel delivered the highlight of the season. While his passion was always on display, he stepped up in the clutch multiple times – including with an 11-foot birdie make worth two points to tie Match 1 in an eventual 6-5 win for Atlanta on Monday night."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“It’s really cool to be a part of something with these guys,” Horschel said. “Team competitions are special. I’ve only been a part of one, the 2022 Presidents Cup. You hear the stories, you know how fun it is ... Just being in something that is competitive, you feel the energy, you feel the nerves. It just brings you closer together. I enjoyed being with these guys and it’s been an absolute blast.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Atlanta was never out of the match despite falling behind 3-0 through 11 holes. The team still had all three Hammers at that point and made good use of them all, winning four points through Holes No. 12-14 for the epic comeback."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"They first cut into the lead at the par-3 12th with their first Hammer throw of the night after Cantlay hit his tee shot to 4 feet. New York declined to make it 3-1. Atlanta threw its second Hammer and added another point at the 13th when Xander Schauffele hit his approach shot in the bunker. New York declined and the lead was down to 3-2."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“You can only really use the Hammer when you get up in holes,” Cantlay said. “We didn’t get up in very many holes until the end and we obviously needed to throw them. ... When we got up in those holes coming down the stretch we threw the Hammer at the right time and got a couple concessions and that got us back in the match. And, obviously, when Billy makes every putt he hits for two points, that’s helpful.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Schauffele gave New York a 3-0 lead with a birdie at the 10th as Atlanta’s struggles on the Green continued. Teammate Lucas Glover, watching from the stands at SoFi Center, was hopeful they could get it going in a bit of foreshadowing."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“We’re still fine,” Glover said. “We’ve got a lot of golf to play.”"}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Things got a bit heated at the par-4 eighth hole, Bluebonnet, when Schauffele threw the Hammer at almost the exact same time Thomas addressed the ball prior to an 11-foot par putt to tie the hole. Rules official Mark Russell declared Thomas had not “totally addressed the ball” prior to the Hammer throw, meaning it would stand. Atlanta ultimately declined after a bit of chirping and New York took a 2-0 lead entering the final hole of Triples."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neither team could gain an edge until the par-3 seventh hole, where Thomas took an aggressive line at the flag and saw his ball roll long into a back left bunker. Schauffele hit his tee shot inside 5 feet and Atlanta eventually conceded the hole to make it 1-0 New York."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"NYGC finished with a 3-4-1 record, embarking on a truly impressive comeback over the second half of the season following an 0-2 start. While they would have liked to have had a few decisions back over the course of Monday and Tuesday’s Finals Series, there was no denying Atlanta’s prowess in Hammer strategy and execution."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“They earned it for sure,” Schauffele said."}]}]

recapTopVideo.videoTitle: Finals Match 2 Highlights: New York Golf Club vs. Atlanta Drive GC
recapTopVideo.shortDescription: In dramatic fashion Atlanta Drive GC come out on top to defeat New York Golf Club 4-3, and win the inaugural SoFi Cup.
